authority.legal_name: HADAG Seetouristik und Fährdienst AG, the City of Hamburg harbour-ferry operator within the HVV
authority.home_waters_label: the Port of Hamburg and the lower Elbe

mandate.summary: HADAG, owned by the City of Hamburg, runs the harbour ferry lines on the Elbe within the HVV public-transport network — carrying around nine million passengers a year on lines 61–75 from Landungsbrücken across the port to Finkenwerder, Blankenese and HafenCity.
current_priorities: Harbour commuter and cross-Elbe ferry service
Full integration in the HVV ticketing and network
Serving the Airbus/Finkenwerder and HafenCity growth areas

policy_targets.decarb_note: Hamburg targets climate neutrality by 2045, and HADAG is testing hybrid and electric ferries — but most of the nine-million-passenger harbour network still runs on diesel.
policy_targets.relevance: Navier is the zero-emission foiling upgrade to a network the City of Hamburg already runs through HADAG — faster, quieter harbour and cross-Elbe lines that relieve the tunnels while delivering the climate-neutral mandate the city has set.

precedent.headline: Public harbour ferries are core HVV transport infrastructure here, not a novelty.
precedent.network: HADAG runs HVV-integrated harbour ferry lines (61–75) from Landungsbrücken across the Port of Hamburg to Finkenwerder, Blankenese, Teufelsbrück and HafenCity, carrying around nine million passengers a year.
precedent.note: Public ferry service is core transport infrastructure here, not a novelty. Navier adds a fast passenger-only foiling layer on the busy corridors.

interpretation_for_navier: Navier is the zero-emission foiling upgrade to a network the City of Hamburg already runs through HADAG — faster, quieter harbour and cross-Elbe lines that relieve the tunnels while delivering the climate-neutral mandate the city has set.

domestic_network.note: Candidate boarding points with APPROXIMATE anchor coordinates [lng, lat] for Grok to snap to real piers/terminals during seal. Coordinates are anchors, not sealed geometry. Core mirrors the authority's live public stops; new/committed/study stops are flagged.

domestic_pairs.rationale: HADAG line 62 — the busiest harbour ferry line, central piers to Finkenwerder.
Line 73 south-bank harbour line to the working port.
Central waterfront line to Altona / Fischmarkt.
Cross-Elbe line linking Finkenwerder to the north bank (Airbus commuters).
Western Elbe line to the Blankenese village.
Cross-Elbe link to the Rüschpark / Airbus side.
HafenCity waterfront line to the Elbphilharmonie.
Cross-harbour line to the Steinwerder theatre and port.

regional_links.note: Domestic-only network across the Port of Hamburg and the lower Elbe. Any down-Elbe links toward Stade/Cuxhaven are secondary and out of scope for this phase.

routing_hazards.instruction: Every domestic leg must be routed through navigable open water with NO land crossings (interior_land_km == 0). Hand-curated waypoints required wherever a breakwater, barrier, bridge pier, reef, headland, naval/exclusion zone or shallows would otherwise be clipped. Use data-clean/uae_hand_waypoints.json format {from, to, waypoints:[[lng,lat]...]}.

hazards.detail: Hamburg is one of Europe's largest container ports — the Elbe fairway is busy with container ships and feeders; cross at marked points and waypoint clear of terminals and turning basins.
The tidal Elbe runs strong currents and the fairway shifts with dredging — follow the marked navigation channel.
The Köhlbrand crossing, harbour locks (Ernst-August-Schleuse) and bridge piers require hand-waypointing.
The western Elbe (Övelgönne, Blankenese) is residential with strict wake limits — no-foil zones near the beaches and landings.
